review:
[h1]The Game Is Dead / Игра Умерла [/h1]

[h3]!Everything written below has been personally verified by me on this account and several others! [/h3]
[h3]!ВСЕ что есть в этом сообщении проверено лично мной на этом и не только аккаунтах! [/h3]
 
For me, this game is dead. The final nail in the coffin for me was the [b]"Behavior Score System"[/b], which does not work as intended. 
[b]Basic examples:[/b]
[list]
    [*] How can you lose your Communication Score if the game itself prevents you from communicating?
    [*] Why is Turbo Mode evaluated and punished the same way as Ranked matches?
    [*] How does sharing or destroying items at the very end of the match (when the Ancient is about to fall) count as negative behavior?
[/list]
Для меня игра умерла окончательно. Последним гвоздем для меня стала [b]"Система порядочности"[/b], которая не работает так как задумано. 
[b]Базовые примеры:[/b]
[list]
    [*] Как можно потерять вежливость, если сама игра запрещает общение?
    [*] Почему Turbo режим оценивают и за него наказывают как за Рейтинговую игру?
    [*] Каким образом передача или ломание предметов под конец игры (трон упадет через мгновение) учитывается как Отрицательные поступки для общей порядочности?
[/list]
[b]Logical flaws:[/b]
[list]
    [*] You can win 9 out of 10 games and get commended by almost every player, but if you receive 4 reports in your last match, your Behavior Score will still drop.
    [*] Some people can use offensive language as much as they want and still keep maximum Behavior and Communication Scores. While others lose EVERYTHING if they write something in the chat!
[/list]
[h3]ADDENDUM: [/h3]
I used to have the maximum Behavior and Communication Scores. At that time, I said whatever I wanted and played however I wanted (except intentional feeding). [b]All this lasted FOR MORE THAN 1 YEAR[/b]. Then I started playing more calmly and respectfully, and as a result, my Behavior Score dropped below 2,000. The fall was not instantaneous, but over a long period of time. I do not know how this happened, but I would like to know! I am absolutely certain that there could not have been any reports based on my past behavior.
[list]
    [*] Why can you permanently lose access to chat when the game already has a mute function for every player and temporary chat bans for players who receive a lot of reports?
    [*] The system itself lowers your Behavior Score for actions that cannot affect the match. It's not Overwatch that does this, but the game itself!
    [*] Reports from players in the same party carry the same weight as reports from solo players. That is, [b]you can be falsely reported[/b] if someone doesn't like you.
[/list]
[b]Логичные и общие ошибки:[/b]
[list]
    [*] Ты можешь выиграть 9 из 10 игр и получить похвалу от всех участников этих игр, но если ты после этого получишь 4 репорта в последней игре ты потеряешь Порядочность!
    [*] Одни могут применять нецензурную брань сколько хотят и у них Максимальная вежливость и порядочность. В то время как другие теряют ВСЕ если напишут что либо в чате!
 [/list]
[h3]ДОПОЛНЕНИЕ: [/h3] 
Раньше я имел максимальную порядочность и вежливость. В это время я говорил все что хотел и дела все что хотел (кроме специальных смертей). [b]Все это продолжалось БОЛЕЕ 1 ГОДА[/b]. Потом я начал играть спокойнее и доброжелательнее и как следствие моя порядочность упала ниже 2 тысяч. Падение было не моментальным, а на протяжении долгого времени. Каким образом это произошло я не знаю, но хотел бы знать! Это [b]абсолютно точно[/b] не могли быть жалобы за прошлое поведение.
[list]
    [*] Почему можно навсегда потерять возможность писать в чат, если для особо токсичных людей уже давно существовала система состоящая из: возможности заглушить любого игрока и запрета писать в конкретно ЭТОЙ игре если на тебя много жалуются!
    [*] Сама система снижает Порядочность за действия не способные помешать игре. Это делает не Патруль, а сама игра!
    [*] Репорты людей состоящих в группе учитываются так же как и соло игроков. То есть [b]тебя могут Оклеветать[/b] если ты не понравился кому то одному.
[/list]
There are still a few minor problems, but all of the above are the main problems that really exist.
Есть еще несколько минорных проблем, но все выше сказанное это основные проблемы, которые правда существуют.

review:
☆☆☆☆☆ 0/5
A horrible MOBA with terrible matchmaking

After more than 100 hours, I can confidently say that Dota 2 is a horrible MOBA overall and cannot come close to competing with League of Legends.

Smurfing is one of the biggest problems. It feels like Valve does not care at all. Experienced players can buy cheap low-ranked accounts, stomp beginners and completely ruin matches.

The pausing system is also ridiculous. People pause constantly, sometimes several times per game, and everyone else is forced to wait.

Communication is often terrible too. Many players only speak Russian and refuse to use English, even when nobody else understands them.

Some items are simply badly designed. Blink Dagger is a perfect example. When you are behind, enemies can camp in the jungle, blink onto you from outside your vision and instantly kill you. It feels like nowhere on the map is safe once your team starts losing.

Other problems include:

Clunky and delayed movement
Extremely slow and overly long matches
Confusing and overdesigned items
Overloaded hero designs
Weak and unsatisfying animations
Bad matchmaking for beginners
No proper party finder
Worse laning than League
Supports fighting carries for farm
Uninteresting map objectives
Smurfs, pauses and poor communication ruining games

People often say Dota 2 is harder or deeper than League. Maybe it is more complicated, but complicated does not automatically mean better. Much of the gameplay feels based on cheesy tactics, invisibility, long stun chains and knowledge checks instead of satisfying mechanical outplays.

League has plenty of problems, but its movement, pacing, laning, clarity and overall gameplay feel far superior.

I gave Dota 2 more than enough chances. The more I played, the worse my opinion became.

I cannot recommend it.

review:
It was the age of stuns, it was the age of silences, it was the hero I wanted, it was the hero I got instead. It was knowledge I moved on and certainty I only imagined, wards that saw and wards I never placed, every choice a wager against a map half-dark.

I've bathed foes in viper's venom, meandered silently with weaver, danced with Shadow Shaman's serpents, dashed the map with Bara. I've been butchered by Pudge, ambushed by Legion Commander. Ensnared by Bane, burned with Ice and Fire by Jakiro. I've Doomed many a player, with satisfaction. I've been unable to evade Windranger and Jugg - and passed the same judgement when I played with these two. I've struck fear from the shadows with Sniper and Muerta. I've pinned many adamant fools with Bristleback. I tango with branches, delve strategically with smoke and get left behind without my trusty pouch of dust.

It is a game that makes some men and unmakes others — anonymity handing back whatever a person already was underneath. I was shortsighted once myself. I've met the ones it unmakes: quick to blame, quick to type what they'd never say aloud. And through all of my own faults and the faults of others, I've met nameless strangers with exceptional co-ordination — those who calculate wins and losses instead of feeling them, who speak, who ping, who guide.

40+ mins. 1 map. 120+ heroes. Endless scenarios. Unlimited fun. There is nothing else like Dota 2, yet.

Dota 2 is probably the best game I've ever played... and the biggest waste of my life at the same time.

You can play your role perfectly, not flame anyone, make all the right calls, and still end up getting reported just because your teammates are tilted or looking for someone to blame. Then suddenly you're in Low Priority for absolutely no reason. It feels like the report system punishes innocent players just because the rest of the team is angry.

Every match is an emotional rollercoaster. You queue thinking, "One game before bed," and somehow it's 3 AM, you've lost 5 games in a row, and you're questioning every life decision you've ever made.

The community can be incredibly toxic, and sometimes it feels like surviving your own teammates is harder than beating the enemy team.

Would I recommend Dota 2?

Absolutely not.

Will I queue again tomorrow?

...Yes.

No matter when you play this game it will have something for you. I played Dota 2 on & off since its initial beta release, I played Dota 1 for 3 years prior to that. I played HoN, a little bit of League, and every little splinter MOBA in between. But something about the craft, the care, the robust landscape & systemic polish of Dota 2 is just special. 

Every hero feels unique and with purpose, even when they are bad or out of flavour. Every update feels rich & fulfilling, even in these latter years where Valve has seemingly abandoned the game. The skins, the items, the couriers, the teleports.. It's all just beautiful dressing on what is a near-perfect baseline game underneath.

And beyond all, the years of stories in this game-- the International, Burning's rise as chinese superstar, the legends of Dota 1 coming & going, James 2GD Harding's controversial but important role in its history, the retirements, the rising hotshot stars, the silly updates & hilarious reveals. This game took up such an immense part of my life that i will forever say: Dota 2 is special.

Title: “A Deep, Competitive Masterpiece — Dota 2 Never Gets Old”

I’ve been playing Dota 2 for years, and it never fails to surprise me. This game is a true masterpiece of strategic depth and competitive intensity. Every match feels unique because of the sheer variety of heroes, items, and playstyles. There’s always something new to learn, no matter how many hours you’ve put in.

The skill ceiling is incredibly high, which is exactly what makes it so rewarding. Pulling off a perfectly coordinated teamfight or executing a clutch play after careful planning gives an unmatched sense of satisfaction. The game rewards smart decision‑making, map awareness, and adaptability — not just mechanical skill.

I also love how the developers keep the game fresh with regular updates, balance changes, and seasonal events. The battle passes and cosmetics are a nice touch, but they never feel pay‑to‑win; the focus stays on the gameplay. Plus, the built‑in tools for watching replays and studying pro matches are fantastic for improving your skills.

The community can be intense (okay, sometimes downright toxic), but when you find good teammates, the cooperation and communication make the victories even sweeter. And for those who prefer a more relaxed experience, there’s a ton of custom content and fun game modes to enjoy.

Graphically, the game still looks great, and the sound design and voice lines add so much character to each hero. Dota 2 isn’t just a game — it’s a whole ecosystem with tournaments, lore, and a passionate global community.

If you’re into strategy, teamwork, and games that really test your mind, Dota 2 is an absolute must‑play. I’d give it 5/5.

review:
Dota 2 is a moderately enjoyable game with a lot of depth, but it's far from being balanced. Some heroes feel noticeably stronger than others, which can make matches frustrating depending on the current meta.

However, the biggest problem isn't the gameplay—it's the behavior score and reporting system. Players can report you for little to no reason, and those reports can significantly lower your behavior score, even if you didn't do anything wrong. Once your behavior score drops, you're forced into matches with toxic players, griefers, and ruiners who intentionally sabotage games. This creates a vicious cycle that's incredibly difficult to escape and makes the overall experience miserable.

A competitive game should reward skill and teamwork, not punish players because of an unreliable reporting system. Unfortunately, this issue overshadows many of the game's strengths.

Because of these problems, I can't recommend Dota 2 to anyone. While the core gameplay has potential, the player experience is too heavily affected by an unfair reporting system and the toxic environment it creates.

review:
If you can use a keyboard and a mouse, if you can read, if you enjoy learning new mechanics, memorizing hundreds of abilities, item interactions, timings, counters, power spikes, map objectives, ward spots, smoke timings, rune control, stacking camps, pulling lanes, and approximately seventeen different ways a single hero can ruin your entire week...

Congratulations.

You are now qualified to complete the tutorial.

Welcome to Dota 2.

A game so beautifully designed that after 1,000 hours you'll still confidently say, "I have absolutely no idea what just happened in that fight."

Other games teach you how to play.

Dota teaches you humility.

Every match is a fresh educational experience where you discover exciting new concepts such as:

* Your hero is apparently useless against their hero.
* Your items were wrong.
* Your skill build was wrong.
* Your positioning was wrong.
* Existing was wrong.

The learning curve isn't a curve. It's a vertical cliff covered in ice, and at the top stands a 12,000 hour veteran laughing while playing a hero you've never seen before.

The ranking system is especially motivating.

Play your heart out for three months to gain 300 MMR.

Lose it all in one weekend because your carry decided farming jungle creeps during the final base defense was "the optimal macro play."

Reach Herald? Congratulations.

Reach Guardian? Impressive.

Reach Crusader? Nice.

Reach Ancient? Great.

Reach Immortal? Wonderful.

You'll still open the match and immediately be informed by your teammates that you are the worst player they have ever witnessed in human history.

The community ensures you never develop dangerous levels of self-confidence.

And the complexity...

Oh, the complexity.

There are heroes with more text in their abilities than some university textbooks.

There are item interactions that require a law degree to understand.

There are mechanics discovered by players ten years after release because apparently everyone collectively forgot they existed.

Every patch note feels less like game balance and more like reading amendments to a country's constitution.

Would I recommend Dota 2?

Absolutely.

If your dream is to suffer for eternity, question every life decision that led you here, develop Stockholm Syndrome with a video game, and after thousands of hours still be permanently trapped in the lower ranks wondering where it all went wrong...

Then Dota 2 is the perfect game for you.

10/10.

review:
Thank You for Making Me Quit — A Dota 2 Review After 10+ Years

Hours played: more than a decade
Recommendation: It's complicated.

Thank you, Valve. Thank you for finally making me quit Dota 2.

I mean that with all the bitterness it deserves, because for me this was never just a game.

For over ten years, Dota was where my friends and I showed up for each other. It was there through the depression, the heartbreaks, the family problems, and the goodbyes when friends left the country to work abroad. When life was falling apart, the queue was still there. We'd load in, pick our heroes, talk trash, lose, win, and somehow feel a little less alone. That was the real game. The matches were just the excuse to keep coming back to each other.

We don't play every day — life doesn't allow that anymore. But when we do get to sit down and queue together, we play it serious. We value teamwork above everything else. That's the whole point for us: five people moving as one, trusting each other to do their part. We played ranked — not to flex, but because ranked was supposed to mean something. It was supposed to be the mode where everyone tried, where you weren't dropped into a lobby with someone treating a serious match like their first day on the game. We queued up as a duo, as a trio, sometimes a full stack of five, and for years that was enough.

But these last months — these last couple of years — every update seems to break something. The matchmaking feels broken in a way it never used to. Smurfs everywhere. Teammates who clearly have no idea what their role is supposed to do. You queue solo, or as two, or as three, and there's almost always that one random filling out the team who doesn't have a clue — and that's all it takes to turn a match into a stress test instead of a game.

That's the part that hurts. Ranked was supposed to fix exactly this. It was supposed to balance the lobby so everyone could actually compete and have fun. Instead it's become the thing causing the stress. The thing draining the fun out of the one place my friends and I went to escape the stress.

Maybe that's the real review here: the game changed. Not the graphics, not the heroes — the feeling. The thing that kept us coming back for ten years quietly stopped being there.

I'm not angry at Dota. I'm grateful for what it gave us. I'm just tired of fighting the matchmaking to get back something that used to come easy.

So thank you, Dota — for the decade, the memories, and the friendships that outlasted every patch.

And thank you, finally, for making it easy to walk away.

review:
Dota 2 is a free to play MOBA that originally started it's life as a mod in Warcraft 3. I want to start off this review by saying that this game is very complex, while you can learn the basics of the game in a few matches the underlying mechanics will take you many hundred to understand. If your looking for something to pick up and play this probably isn't it unless your willing to learn over a hundred hours or more. The game is free to play but unlike other free to play games all purchases in Dota are purely cosmetic and add no advantage or pay to win mechanics, as more games should be.

For those unfamiliar a MOBA consists a 5v5 game on a 3 lane map. 2 heroes go top and bottom and 1 usually will go middle. There a certain heroes who excel in certain roles that you will eventually learn over time. In recent years Dota has added a new player learning section which is great for people new to MOBAs or Dota in general. It covers not just a MOBA but also mechanics specific to Dota I will take about later. A typical match in Dota will last between 30 and 75 minutes but have lasted all the way up to close to over 3 hours in a pro level match before. There are so many different mechanics that have an impact on a match that no 2 matches will ever feel the same.

For the majority of my review I will be comparing Dota 2 to it's main competitor League of Legends and then I will get into other details on Dota after. For starters Dota 2  has far less heroes than League of Legends at 127 currently compared to 171 in League of Legends. Despite needing to learn more heroes League of Legends is actually an easier MOBA to play, however because of that fact it's also boring and games are pretty predictable. If you lose the laning phase it's very hard to come back in League of Legends because there are no game changing items you can buy. In Dota 2 there are items such as Black King Bar (BKB) which makes you 100% immune to magic damage, which is 1 of the 3 types of damage from hero abilities in Dota. There are other items to like the blink dagger which allows you to teleport a certain distance around you to gank enemies. There are many different items in Dota that can allow you to come back from a few deaths at the start of the game. You also don't lose gold when you die in league making getting items a little easier where as in Dota you lose a % of gold and the other team gets gold each kill.

In League of Legends the laning phase also changes to 2 bottom 1 top 1 mid and 1 jungle right away which is roaming the map and killing the mobs for gold and xp. In Dota even the high damage carry heroes need a few levels before being able to farm the jungle. In League of Legends you also don't have camp stacking. In Dota when farming jungle or in the early game the support heroes and sometimes mid will go around and pull jungle mobs from there spawn. If they are out of the spawn box at the start of each new minute a new stack will spawn and if you run away from the pulled mobs they will return effectively leaving 2 groups on the jungle camp. The person who makes the stacked camp gets XP and Gold once those are killed even if not by themselves. This is just another big mechanic in Dota that allows you to come back or get ahead of the other team.

Dota has much more mechanics to watch for in the laning phase as well such as "Denying" or killing your own creeps before the other team does. This will give the other team half the XP they normally would and denies them getting gold from the last hit. Both games feature the same last hit mechanics requiring you to be the final person to hit a creep to their death to get any gold. However in league there is no turn rate so u don't need to face the creep to hit it where as in Dota each hero has its own timing to turn and face the creep and it's own timing to hit the creep you will need to account for. Again this is just another way to get an advantage back to your team if you die in the laning phase, just getting more last hits and denying the other teams gold and XP will help.

Lastly Dota 2 is harder because you can't see over stairs. The game uses a 3D model where league you can basically see anywhere expect hiding in a bush or something. Enemies can be waiting at the top of the stairs and you wouldn't know without climbing up or placing wards to see. This makes movement very different in Dota and can lead to some bad deaths and emphasizes the importance of placing wards for vision. Dota also applies a 25% chance to miss your target such as a creep if they are above you, this is most common for the midlaner who fights between 2 stairs.

While these mechanics make the game far more challenging to play and learn, they do create many options for a game to turn out and for that I rate it a 10/10 for game mechanics. The game gets a new update about once a month constantly balancing heroes and changing the content and mechanics in the game. This is frustrating to learn all the time but also keeps the game ever changing and well balanced as it's hard to make 127 heroes feel perfectly balanced. It also shows the devs care a lot about the game.

Dota 2 has had a huge esports scene in the past but for some reason they decided to make a couple large tournaments throughout the year rather than host The International (TI) as a big event. Personally I think this is a 1/10. As someone who didn't play much Dota in the past the big TI prize pools caught my eye and brought in new players like myself to see what this game is all about. I think if Valve wants to make different tournaments have decent prize pools go back to the old model of community funded battle passes and cosmetics to go back to the prize pool and just host multiple passes throughout the year for different tournaments. The tournaments are still large but it does attract media away from Dota and towards other titles with higher payouts as well as gamers and teams trying to make a profitable living. Look how many people were playing Fortnite and head of the game over their 100M dollar tournament years ago. Steam should be advertising the tournament on their store page when it was 20-40M for the TI. It's a big deal and the qualifier rounds and main tournament coverage should be posted to attract new viewers and players.

Overall Dota is a great game, it falls in line with Valves other games like Counter Strike in the fact that it is easy to run. Valve also has 2 giants in the market making them a ton of revenue on top of steam sales commissions that this game isn't going anywhere anytime soon. I would recommend playing this game and trying to learn it for 100 hours which will allow you to finally play the ranked mode and get matched with people around the same skill as you. Don't worry about people getting mad with you while you learn, and maybe try a couple bot games first before unranked. This game is challenging but is super fun.

review:
The communication score system doesn't seem to reflect actual toxicity at all. For years, I've had between 10k and 12k behaviour score chilling in my games playing all roles. My approach was always simple: mute toxic players and focus on playing and try win. Yet recently I'm losing anywhere from 300 to 600 communication score every 15 games with no clear explanation.

When I check my match data in game stats on steam, I see only 4–6 reports across that period. At this point, it feels like some players enter games and report everyone regardless of what happened. I've unbinded chat key and turned chat off completely to try get it back up, yet its no good ! This was because I suspected even typing positive stuff was causing it to fall.

I don't get HOW CAN COMMS SCORE GO DOWN IF YOU DON'T EVEN TALK AND UNBINDED CHAT KEY AND HAD CHAT OFF ?

The system is actually dogshit and broken, I used to say the same sitting on my high horse at 12k, but no these 'toxic' people where right about everything and its killing the game.
 
Since reports are effectively unlimited, why do such a small number of reports carry so much weight? If you happen to get a few frustrated teammates every 15 games, you can lose over 1,500 communication score surprisingly quickly, which feels wrong considering I've read the max you can get back is 300 per 15 ? (Haven't even broke even yet to test this) I see people celebrating gains of 100–150 score on reddit as if that's a meaningful recovery rate. The system feels far more punishing than rewarding and designed to force you onto a new account. 

Once your communication score falls below 11k, it becomes extremely difficult to maintain. Mine started declining only after dropping from around 11k, and now it feels like unless you're comfortably above 11k, your account is on a timer.

Someone can use scripts or cheats for years without anyone caring, reports do nothing for this ? Every Smurfy Arc, Tinker I've met with blatant scripts is unbanned to this day. They probably have 12k behaviour so who cares right!

review:
used to enjoy Dota 2, but the ranked system has become one of the most frustrating parts of the game.

The MMR system feels like it only punishes players instead of rewarding improvement. You can play well, carry your team, and still lose because of one bad teammate. A single game can ruin hours of progress.

The Behavior Score and Communication Score system also feels unfair and unclear. You can try to play normally, but one bad match, a few reports, or arguments with teammates can lower your score and put you with even worse players. It feels like the system does not always understand the difference between a toxic player and someone just having a bad game.

The community is one of the biggest problems. Too many games are ruined by people flaming, blaming teammates, giving up early, or intentionally ruining the match. A good team game becomes stressful because you spend more time dealing with players than actually enjoying the game.

Dota 2 has amazing heroes, deep strategy, and great gameplay, but the matchmaking and player behavior systems need a lot of improvement. New players especially will have a hard time staying interested when every match feels like a punishment.

Great game idea, but the ranked experience and community make it hard to enjoy.

review:
I want to say that this used to be the best game. It was Valve's number one title and one of the greatest competitive games ever made. But for some reason, it feels like you've deliberately decided to kill it.

First, why was All Random removed from the game? Was it bothering anyone? Why are you removing features that were already implemented and enjoyed by players?

Second, as a regular player who doesn't want to play ranked because every other match is filled with boosters who are clearly above my skill level, I mostly play Turbo. So why am I still being matched against players who are significantly better than me?
When are you finally going to create proper skill-based matchmaking? Why am I so often placed against players who are on a completely different level?

Third, your so-called "50% system" is one of the worst ideas imaginable. The most enjoyable matches in Dota are games where both teams are evenly matched in skill. Because of this system, those games only happen about one out of ten times.
Instead, your matchmaking seems to put one or several weak players on the enemy team so that I can win. But that's not fun. Winning because the other team has inexperienced players isn't satisfying.
On the other hand, when the weak player ends up on my team and we're facing much stronger opponents, that's equally terrible. Nobody enjoys getting stomped because the teams are unbalanced.
As a result, this "50% system" is one of the worst possible solutions to the matchmaking problem. Players don't want forced win rates - they want fair and balanced games.

Fourth, why did you ruin The International prize pools? Every year The International feels less exciting and less important than it used to. Why not bring back the system that allowed players to contribute to and increase the prize pool? That was one of the things that made TI special and helped create the biggest event in esports.

Fifth, why are balance changes being handled by people who, judging by the results, seem to have little understanding of the game? Many recent patches feel disconnected from what players actually want. Bring back the people who were working on the game 10 years ago!

And finally, why is there no role queue in unranked matchmaking? If role selection improves match quality in ranked games, why can't unranked players have the same option?
